item.title: Escambia County Schools Removed 22 Books in 2024-25 School Year
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County schools removed 22 books from their collections during the 2024-25 school year, according to data shared on social media during Banned Books Week. The removals place Escambia third among Florida counties tracked in the report, behind Clay County with 282 removals and Polk County with 53. Santa Rosa County, which borders Escambia,…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County schools removed 22 books from their collections during the 2024-25 school year, according to data shared on social media during Banned Books Week. The removals place Escambia third among Florida counties tracked in the report, behind Clay County with 282 removals and Polk County with 53.

Santa Rosa County, which borders Escambia, had 17 book removals during the same period. Other Northwest Florida counties showed lower removal numbers: Bay County reported 10 removals and Marion County also reported 10.

The data was compiled and shared by Casey Reads, a social media account focused on book access issues, as part of Banned Books Week awareness. The report does not specify which titles were removed or the reasons behind individual removals.

item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old Cantonment resident was taken into custody following a domestic disturbance that involved a knife and ended with a foot pursuit with Escambia County Sheriff's Office deputies.

Deangelo Jerrell Bolden was arrested and charged with felony battery by strangulation, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill, grand theft, criminal mischief, and resisting an officer without violence. Details of the initial dispute and circumstances leading to the foot pursuit were not immediately disclosed.

The case remains under investigation by ECSO.

item.content:encoded: Florida drivers are catching a break at the pump this week after oil prices pulled back from recent highs, according to AAA. The decline reflects broader movements in crude oil markets that have eased pressure on retail fuel costs across the state.

item.title: Downtown Pensacola Paid Parking Resumes After Construction Pause
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Paid parking enforcement returns to downtown Pensacola today, according to reporting from North Escambia, marking the end of a temporary suspension tied to the Reimagine Palafox construction project. The resumption brings several changes for drivers navigating the downtown core. Officials have introduced new free parking days, adjusted hourly…
item.content:encoded:
Paid parking enforcement returns to downtown Pensacola today, according to reporting from North Escambia, marking the end of a temporary suspension tied to the Reimagine Palafox construction project.

The resumption brings several changes for drivers navigating the downtown core. Officials have introduced new free parking days, adjusted hourly rates, and localized rule modifications to reflect the ongoing construction impact. The city is also rolling out an initial grace period where drivers will receive warnings rather than immediate citations as the system ramps back up.

Drivers who park downtown should review updated signage and rate schedules to avoid violations during this transition phase.

item.content:encoded: The Town of Century has rolled out a new online payment option for residents looking to pay their water, sewer, sanitation, and natural gas bills. The system is secure and available to all Century utility customers.

item.content:encoded: The University of West Florida Argos suffered a lopsided 35-7 loss to Abilene Christian on Saturday night in their latest test competing at the Division I FCS level. Despite entering the game ranked No. 17 nationally, UWF couldn't overcome a dominant first half by the Wildcats, who built a four-touchdown lead by halftime and cruised to victory at Wildcat Stadium. The result underscores the growing competitive challenge facing the Argos as they continue their transition into FCS football. Abilene Christian, a two-time United Athletic Conference champion, improved on its 1-4 season record with the dominant performance.

item.content:encoded:
Military veterans and their families in North Escambia now have regular access to local assistance without traveling far from home. National Veteran Service Officer Tim Chandler will hold weekly office hours every Tuesday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Century Chamber of Commerce building, 7811 North Century Boulevard, beginning this week.

The move brings veteran services directly to the northern part of Escambia County, making it easier for local veterans to access support with benefits, claims, and other services in person. Chandler's office will operate consistently on Tuesdays, providing a predictable schedule for veterans seeking assistance.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Parks and Recreation is moving forward with a routine maintenance project at Lake Stone in Century, replacing aging wooden piers and railings to keep the popular fishing destination safe and functional.

The pier has been temporarily closed while crews handle the rehabilitation work. Lake Stone Campground, situated at 801 West Highway 4, spans 100 acres and serves the community as both a campground and boat ramp facility, making the pier a key amenity for anglers and water enthusiasts in North Escambia.

County Parks and Recreation did not specify a timeline for completion of the project or when the pier would reopen to the public.

item.title: TSA PreCheck Members Can Now Visit Gates at Pensacola Airport Without Flying
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola International Airport has launched a new program that lets approved visitors accompany passengers to the gate area—no plane ticket required. The initiative, called Gateside by TSA PreCheck, allows people with active TSA PreCheck memberships to clear security checkpoint screening without a boarding pass, according to reporting from North…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport has launched a new program that lets approved visitors accompany passengers to the gate area—no plane ticket required. The initiative, called Gateside by TSA PreCheck, allows people with active TSA PreCheck memberships to clear security checkpoint screening without a boarding pass, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The program is designed to give families and friends more time together before departure, eliminating the need for visitors to watch travelers disappear through the security line. It's a convenience feature that several major U.S. airports already offer, and now travelers using Pensacola International can take advantage of the same benefit.

To participate, visitors must have an active TSA PreCheck membership and go through the standard security screening process at the airport. The program applies to the gate areas but does not permit access to other restricted airport zones.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County Master Gardeners held a workshop at the Molino Branch Library focused on hobby greenhouse management for local gardeners. The session covered practical strategies for setting up and maintaining backyard greenhouses on a budget, along with preparation tips as the region heads into cooler fall and winter months. The workshop provided attendees with guidance on economical approaches to hobby greenhouse gardening, a growing interest among home gardeners in Northwest Florida looking to extend their growing season or protect plants from seasonal weather changes.
